items.title: Federal rule: your balance can’t expire for 5 years
items.summary: Under the federal Credit CARD Act and Regulation E, money on a gift card stays good for at least 5 years from the date the card was bought or last loaded. Inactivity fees are limited, and a card that expires while the money is still valid must be replaced at no charge.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Funds must stay valid for at least 5 years after the card was issued or money was last loaded. If the plastic card shows an earlier date, the issuer must give you a replacement card or the remaining balance at no charge.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: Dormancy, inactivity or service fees are allowed only after 12 months with no activity, no more than one fee in any calendar month, and only if the fee amount and frequency are printed on the card.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Store gift cards, gift certificates and general-use (network-branded) prepaid gift cards sold to consumers. Not covered: reloadable prepaid cards not marketed as gifts, loyalty or promotional cards, paper-only certificates, phone cards, cards not marketed to the general public, and event or venue admission cards.

fields.label: State law
fields.value: States may give you more time or stronger protections. The CFPB notes your state may provide additional rights.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: 12 CFR § 1005.20 (Regulation E, implementing the Credit CARD Act of 2009)

items.title: If a store closes, goes bankrupt or won’t take your card
items.summary: The FTC says a card from a company that closed or filed for bankruptcy may be worth less than you expect. Call the company, or a competitor, to ask whether they are still redeeming the cards. If a card is refused as expired or fees were deducted, contact the issuer and ask it to honor the card or reverse the fees.

fields.label: Store closed or bankrupt
fields.value: Call the company or its competitor to find out if they are redeeming the cards. If a nearby store closes, the card may be harder to use. The CFPB notes a card from a retailer that went out of business may not be redeemable.

fields.label: Card refused or fees taken
fields.value: Contact the company that issued the card. Ask whether the card can still be honored or the fees reversed. Under federal rules, if the funds are still valid, a new card must be issued at no cost.

fields.label: Keep
fields.value: The card’s terms, the original receipt and the card ID number.

fields.label: Complain
fields.value: Report bad business practices to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. The CFPB takes complaints about prepaid cards and sends them to the company for a response.

items.title: Arkansas: no fees for 2 years
items.summary: Arkansas bars dormancy, inactivity and service fees on gift certificates, store gift cards and general-use prepaid cards for 2 years after issuance, and bars expiration sooner than 2 years. The federal 5-year rule still applies on top.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No dormancy, inactivity or service fees within 2 years of issuance or sale. Any post-sale fee after that must be printed on the card in at least 10-point type with the amount, what triggers it, how often it applies and whether inactivity triggers it.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration earlier than 2 years from issuance or sale (federal law requires at least 5 years). Any expiration date must be printed clearly on the card.

fields.label: Terms
fields.value: Disclosed terms may not be changed after purchase unless the change benefits you.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates, store gift cards and general-use prepaid cards.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Ark. Code § 4-88-703

items.title: California: cash back under $15
items.summary: California store gift cards don’t expire and can’t carry service fees. Since April 1, 2026, any gift card balance under $15 must be paid out in cash when you ask. Before that date the limit was $10.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: Balances under $15 must be redeemed for cash on request. Stores must honor the $15 rule even if the card still says $10. A 2026 law (SB 1078, effective January 1, 2027) lets businesses keep using cards printed before April 1, 2026 through December 31, 2028 if they post a point-of-sale notice that balances under $15 are redeemable for cash.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Selling a gift certificate or gift card with an expiration date is unlawful. A card sold without one is valid until redeemed or replaced. Exceptions: free promotional or loyalty cards, discounted or donated fundraising cards that expire within 30 days, and cards for perishable food, all with the date printed on the front.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No service or dormancy fees. Only exception: a dormancy fee of up to $1 a month on a reloadable card after 24 months of no activity when $5 or less remains, and only if the fee is printed on the card.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates, gift cards and electronic gift cards usable at one seller or affiliated sellers. Cards usable at multiple unaffiliated sellers are not covered if any expiration date is printed on the card.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1749.45, 1749.5 (as amended by SB 22, Stats. 2025, ch. 207)

items.title: Colorado: cash back at $5 or less
items.summary: Colorado store gift cards can’t carry service, dormancy, inactivity, maintenance or any other fee. When $5 or less is left, the issuer must redeem it for cash if you ask.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: If the remaining value is $5 or less, the issuer must redeem it for cash on request (since August 11, 2010).

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: Selling a gift card with a service, dormancy, inactivity, maintenance or any other type of fee is unlawful.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Colorado’s gift card law sets no expiration rule of its own; the federal 5-year rule applies.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards usable at one seller or affiliated sellers. Not covered: cards usable at multiple unaffiliated sellers, paper-only certificates, free promotional or loyalty cards, government-issued cards, prepaid phone or technology cards, and discounted cards sold to employers or charities for fundraising.

items.title: Connecticut: gift cards never expire
items.summary: Connecticut bars expiration dates on gift certificates and gift cards, and bars dormancy, inactivity or similar fees. If a business already reported your unused balance to the state Treasurer, it can still honor the card and get reimbursed.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No person may sell or issue a gift certificate subject to an expiration date, and the card or its terms may not even suggest one.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: Holders of gift certificates may not impose dormancy, inactivity, abandoned-property or similar fees or penalties, or suggest such fees in the terms.

fields.label: Unclaimed property
fields.value: A business that reported the unredeemed value to the Treasurer may still honor the card and seek reimbursement from the Treasurer.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates as defined in Conn. Gen. Stat. § 3-56a.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 42-460, 3-65c

items.title: Florida: no expiration, no fees
items.summary: Gift certificates and credit memos sold in Florida may not have an expiration date or any post-sale fee, including service, dormancy, account maintenance or cash-out fees.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration date or expiration period. Exceptions: certificates given as a charitable contribution (3 years or more) or as an employee incentive (1 year or more) if the date is disclosed in writing, free loyalty or promotional certificates, and certificates tied to a limited-duration convention, vacation or event.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No post-sale charges or fees of any kind.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates bought for money and credit memos issued for returned merchandise. Not covered: cards issued by a financial institution or money services business that work at multiple unaffiliated merchants, prepaid calling cards, tickets, and manufacturer or retailer coupons.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Fla. Stat. § 501.95

items.title: Hawaii: cash back under $5
items.summary: Hawaii store gift cards must be honored for at least 5 years (paper certificates 2 years), can’t carry dormancy or inactivity fees, and a remaining balance under $5 must be paid out in cash.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: If less than $5 remains, the issuer must redeem the remaining value for cash.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Any expiration date must be at least 5 years after issuance (2 years for paper-only certificates) and must be shown on the certificate or, for electronic cards, on the sales receipt. A certificate with no expiration date is valid forever.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No service fees, including dormancy or inactivity fees. A one-time activation or issuance fee may not exceed the lesser of 10% of face value or $5.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates and cards sold by restaurants and retailers for full face value. Not covered: free loyalty, award or promotional cards, discounted certificates, phone-only cards, reloadable cards not marketed as gifts, cards not marketed to the public, and venue-admission cards.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Haw. Rev. Stat. § 481B-13

items.title: Illinois: 5 years and no post-purchase fees
items.summary: Store gift certificates and gift cards sold in Illinois can’t expire sooner than 5 years after issuance and can’t carry any post-purchase fee. The face value may not shrink for non-use.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration date earlier than 5 years after issuance (certificates issued on or after January 1, 2008). Exceptions: free promotional or loyalty certificates, discounted fundraising certificates that expire within 30 days, and certificates for a food product.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No post-purchase fees. You may not be penalized in any way for non-use or late redemption.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards, electronic gift cards, stored-value cards and store credit slips usable at one seller. Not covered: cards usable at multiple sellers, prepaid phone or technology cards, and free award cards.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: 815 ILCS 505/2SS

items.title: Kentucky: no fees before the card expires
items.summary: Kentucky bars dormancy, latency, administrative or other fees that reduce a gift card’s value until the card’s expiration date has passed. A card sold without a printed expiration date is valid until redeemed or replaced.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No service charges or fees that reduce what you can redeem until the expiration date has passed. A violator owes the cardholder the amount lost, court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Kentucky’s own minimum is 1 year after issuance; the federal rule requires at least 5 years. A card sold without an expiration date printed on it is valid until redeemed or replaced.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards and certificates issued by a merchant for full payment. Not covered: prepaid phone cards, bank-issued general-use prepaid cards usable at multiple merchants or ATMs, and free promotional cards.

items.title: Louisiana: 5 years, no dormancy fees
items.summary: Louisiana gift certificates and gift cards can’t expire sooner than 5 years after issuance and can’t carry service or dormancy fees. A one-time handling fee of up to $1 is the only fee allowed.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Any expiration date must be at least 5 years after issuance and printed in capital letters in at least 10-point font. A certificate sold without an expiration date is valid until redeemed or replaced.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No service fee, including dormancy fees. A one-time handling fee may not exceed $1 per certificate.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates, gift cards, electronic cards with a banked value and merchandise credits. Not covered: free loyalty or promotional certificates, discounted or donated fundraising certificates, and general-use prepaid cards issued by federally insured banks.

items.title: Massachusetts: 7 years and cash back on small balances
items.summary: Massachusetts gift certificates and gift cards must stay valid for at least 7 years. Once you have used 90% of a non-reloadable card, or $5.00 or less is left on a reloadable card, you can choose cash for the rest. Fees that reduce the balance are banned.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: Non-reloadable card: after at least 90% of the face value has been used, you may take the remaining balance in cash. Reloadable card: when $5.00 or less remains, you may take it in cash. A card with a zero balance is void.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Valid for at least 7 years from issuance; the issue and expiration dates must be shown. A certificate without a clearly marked expiration date is redeemable forever.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: Selling a gift certificate with dormancy, latency, administrative, periodic, service or similar fees that reduce the redeemable amount is punishable by a fine of up to $300 per violation.

fields.label: Refusal
fields.value: A seller who refuses to redeem a gift certificate before its expiration date can be fined up to $300.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates and gift cards sold in Massachusetts.

items.title: Maryland: no expiration or fees for 4 years
items.summary: A Maryland store gift certificate or gift card may not expire or carry any fee within 4 years of purchase. A card sold in violation stays valid with no expiration and no fees.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration within 4 years after purchase. Any expiration or fee that applies after 4 years must be printed clearly in at least 10-point type on the card, a permanent sticker or the envelope.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No fee or charge of any kind within 4 years after purchase.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Paper or plastic certificates sold for a cash value or issued as store credit for returns. Not covered: network-branded cards usable at multiple unaffiliated sellers (those must print any expiration date and fees in 10-point type under § 14-1320), prepaid phone, internet or tech-support cards, coupons, and free award cards.

items.title: Maine: cash back under $5
items.summary: Maine gift cards and gift obligations can’t be subject to a time limit on redemption, and no fees may be charged other than a disclosed issuance fee. If you redeem in person and less than $5 is left, the merchant must refund it in cash on request.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: When a gift card or gift obligation is redeemed in person and less than $5 remains, the merchant must refund the balance in cash if you ask. Not required for cards with an initial value of $5 or less, promotional cards, or cards given as a refund for returns without a receipt.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No period of limitation may be imposed on your right to redeem.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No fees or charges, except a transaction fee at issuance (and, for stored-value cards, when value is added) that is disclosed in writing before issuance. The fee limits do not apply to cards usable at multiple unaffiliated merchants.

fields.label: Unclaimed property
fields.value: Maine may treat unused value as abandoned after 2 years (gift obligations) or 3 years (stored-value cards) of inactivity, but that does not limit your right to redeem.

items.title: Michigan: 5 years, no inactivity fees, must be accepted
items.summary: Michigan gift certificates and gift cards can’t expire in less than 5 years and can’t carry inactivity or service fees. Retailers, including liquidators running a going-out-of-business sale, may not refuse a valid card for personal purchases.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: A retailer may not sell a gift certificate that expires within less than 5 years.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No inactivity fee or other service fee for holding or using a gift certificate. A fee paid at purchase that is not deducted from the face value is allowed.

fields.label: Acceptance
fields.value: A retailer may not refuse a gift certificate for personal, family or household purchases, restrict its use against its stated terms, change its terms after issuance, or refuse to apply a small remaining balance toward a larger purchase. This also binds anyone running a closeout or going-out-of-business sale for the retailer.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards and certificates usable at one retailer, an affiliated group, or multiple unaffiliated retailers. Not covered: bank general-use prepaid cards, payroll cards, prepaid phone cards, health or dependent-care accounts, discount programs, free promotional certificates, and certain airline vouchers.

items.title: Minnesota: gift cards can’t expire or carry fees
items.summary: It is unlawful to sell a gift certificate or gift card in Minnesota that is subject to an expiration date or to any service fee, including dormancy fees.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: None allowed.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No service fees, including dormancy fees.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards, stored-value cards and store cards issued for payment. Not covered: free loyalty or promotional cards, cards sold below face value to employers or nonprofits for fundraising, employer recognition cards, bank-issued multi-merchant cards that disclose any expiration date and fees, debit cards tied to a deposit account, and prepaid calling cards.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Minn. Stat. § 325G.53

items.title: Montana: cash back under $5
items.summary: A Montana gift certificate is valid until redeemed and does not terminate. No fee may reduce its value, and when less than $5 is left on a card that started above $5, the issuer must redeem it for cash on request.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: If the original value was more than $5 and less than $5 remains, the issuer or seller must redeem the remainder for cash when you ask.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: A gift certificate is valid until redemption and does not terminate.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No fee may reduce the value, including dormancy fees.

fields.label: Bankruptcy
fields.value: If the issuer or seller declares bankruptcy after selling the certificate, the law treats the certificate as trust property of the holder. The value belongs to the holder, not the issuer.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Mont. Code Ann. § 30-14-108

items.title: North Dakota: store gift cards good for 6 years, no fees
items.summary: Store gift cards and gift certificates bought in North Dakota must be valid for at least 6 years from purchase, and no monthly or annual service or maintenance fees may be deducted.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration or redemption deadline before 6 years after purchase, and no wording suggesting an earlier date.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No additional monthly or annual service or maintenance fees.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards and certificates bought for use at a specific store or service. The state attorney general says the law does not apply to universal prepaid cards with a Visa or MasterCard logo. Free promotional cards must disclose any restrictions in writing.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: N.D. Cent. Code § 51-29-02

items.title: New Jersey: cash back under $5, funds don’t expire
items.summary: For New Jersey stored value cards sold since December 1, 2012, the funds are valid until redeemed and do not expire. If less than $5 is left after a purchase, the merchant must refund it in cash on request. No dormancy fee may be charged within 24 months of sale or last use.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: Since September 1, 2012, a balance under $5 left after redemption must be refunded in cash at your request. Not required for non-reloadable cards sold for $5 or less, rewards cards, cards given instead of a refund, venue-admission cards, donated or discounted nonprofit cards, or cards usable at multiple unaffiliated merchants. Each refusal carries a $500 penalty plus restitution.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Funds on cards sold on or after December 1, 2012 are valid until redemption and do not expire, even if the plastic card shows an expiration date allowed by federal law.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No dormancy fee within 24 months of sale or the most recent use; after that, no more than $2.00 per month, and only if disclosed in 10-point type with a phone number.

fields.label: Unclaimed property
fields.value: A card with no activity for 5 years is presumed abandoned under state unclaimed property law.

items.title: New Mexico: 60 months and no fees
items.summary: New Mexico gift certificates can’t expire sooner than 60 months after issuance, and the issuer may not charge any fee for selling, redeeming or replacing them beyond the initial purchase price.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration date less than 60 months after issuance. If no expiration date is conspicuously stated, the certificate has no expiration date and is valid until redeemed or replaced.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No fees of any kind for sale, redemption or replacement other than an initial charge not exceeding face value. The value may not be reduced by service or dormancy fees.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates and electronic gift cards usable with a single seller or affiliated sellers, and merchandise credits. Not covered: cards usable at multiple unaffiliated sellers, free promotional cards, certain discounted employer or nonprofit certificates, phone-only or bank debit devices, and certificates issued by banks, credit unions or licensed money transmitters.

items.title: New York: 9 years, no fees, cash back under $5
items.summary: Gift cards sold in New York can’t expire sooner than 9 years after issuance or last load, can’t carry activation, dormancy, service or other fees (except a one-time fee of up to $9 on open-loop bank-type cards), and a store gift card balance under $5 must be redeemed for cash on request.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: A store (non-open-loop, non-promotional) gift card with a remaining balance under $5 may be redeemed for cash on request.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Any expiration date on a non-promotional gift card must be at least 9 years after issuance or the date funds were last loaded, whichever is later, and must be stated clearly on the card.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No activation, retroactive, redemption, service, dormancy, latency, administrative, handling, access, periodic, renewal, reloading or other fees. Only exception: a one-time activation or issuance fee of up to $9 on an open-loop (multi-merchant) card. The balance may not decline for non-use.

fields.label: Acceptance
fields.value: Issuers, and businesses running closing-out or going-out-of-business sales, may not refuse gift cards or store credits for personal, family or household purchases, including sale or liquidation goods. Terms may not be changed after issuance.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates and gift cards, including open-loop cards. Not covered: cards linked to deposit accounts, transit cards, prepaid phone cards, health or dependent-care accounts, disclosed discount programs, and payroll cards. Promotional cards issued free have their own rules.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: N.Y. Gen. Bus. Law § 396-i

items.title: Ohio: no fees for 2 years
items.summary: Ohio bars any service charge or fee that reduces a gift card’s value within 2 years of issuance, and bars selling a card that expires sooner than 2 years. The federal 5-year rule still applies on top.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No dormancy, latency, administrative or similar fees within 2 years after issuance. A violator owes you the lost value, court costs and reasonable attorney’s fees.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration date less than 2 years after issuance (federal law requires at least 5 years). A card sold without an expiration date is valid until redeemed or replaced.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards issued by a merchant for future goods, services, credit or money. Not covered: free promotional or loyalty cards, certain fundraising and employer cards, cards usable at multiple unaffiliated sellers, and prepaid calling cards.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Ohio Rev. Code § 1349.61

items.title: Oregon: no expiration, cash back under $5
items.summary: Oregon gift cards can’t expire or lose value over time, and no inactivity, maintenance or service fee may be charged. Once you have used the card at least once and less than $5 is left, the business must redeem it for cash on request.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: After at least one purchase, a remaining balance under $5 is redeemable for cash (money or a check) from the business named on the card, since January 1, 2012. The Oregon DOJ describes the limit as $5 or less. Not required for free promotional cards, phone-company cards, or cards redeemed to an online account.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration date, except a card sold at a discount may expire if the date is printed in at least 10-point type and is at least 30 days after the sale.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No fee of any kind related to the card, and the value may not decline over time or for lack of use.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift cards under Oregon’s gift card law. Prepaid calling cards and cellphone minutes are not gift cards.

items.title: Rhode Island: no expiration, no fees, cash under $1
items.summary: Rhode Island bars expiration dates, redemption time limits, surcharges and service or maintenance fees on gift certificates. Any unused balance must be reissued to you, or paid in cash when it is under $1.00.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration date and no time limit on redemption. The certificate or its terms may not even suggest one.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No surcharge and no monthly or annual service or maintenance fees.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: An unused balance under $1.00 must be paid in cash. Larger balances must be reissued on a certificate for the unused amount.

fields.label: Unclaimed property
fields.value: Because redemption is unlimited, the state does not escheat the funds paid for unredeemed gift certificates.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates sold in Rhode Island. Not covered: free promotional or loyalty certificates (restrictions must be disclosed in writing), prepaid wireless cards, cards issued by state-chartered banks or credit unions, and third-party cards usable at multiple unaffiliated merchants that follow federal disclosure guidelines.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: R.I. Gen. Laws § 6-13-12

items.title: Tennessee: no fees for 2 years
items.summary: Tennessee bars issuance fees and any service, dormancy, latency or administrative fee that reduces a gift certificate’s value within 2 years of issuance, and bars expiration sooner than 2 years. The federal 5-year rule still applies on top.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No issuance fee, and no fees that reduce the redeemable amount within 2 years of issuance.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: No expiration less than 2 years after issuance (federal law requires at least 5 years). A certificate or prepaid card sold without an expiration date is valid until redeemed or replaced.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates and merchant prepaid cards. Not covered: free promotional or loyalty certificates, discounted fundraising or employer certificates, employee recognition cards, prepaid calling cards, and prepaid cards usable at multiple unaffiliated merchants or ATMs.

fields.label: Law
fields.value: Tenn. Code § 47-18-127

items.title: Vermont: 5 years, no fees, cash under $1
items.summary: Vermont gift certificates must keep their paid value for at least 5 years from issuance or last load, and after expiration the unused value must be returned to you on request. All fees are banned, and a balance under $1.00 is redeemable in cash on demand.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: If the remaining value is less than $1.00, the certificate is redeemable in cash on demand.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: Paid value is valid for at least 5 years from issuance or last load, whichever is later. A certificate without a clearly marked expiration date has none. After expiration, the unused paid value must be returned to the holder on request.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: Dormancy, latency, issuance, redemption, administrative and other service fees are prohibited. A licensed money transmitter, bank or credit union may charge a one-time issuance fee of up to $10 on a prepaid access card.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates sold in Vermont (8 V.S.A. chapter 81).

items.title: Washington: no expiration, cash back under $5
items.summary: Washington gift certificates and gift cards can’t have an expiration date, fees or dormancy charges and stay valid until redeemed. If less than $5 is left after a purchase, the issuer must redeem it for cash on request.

fields.label: Cash back
fields.value: When a purchase leaves less than $5 on the card, the remaining value must be redeemable in cash on demand. For $5 or more, the issuer may give cash or a new certificate.

fields.label: Expiration
fields.value: None. A gift certificate is valid until redeemed or replaced. Exceptions: certificates issued under an awards or loyalty program, or donated to a charity, may carry a clearly disclosed expiration date.

fields.label: Fees
fields.value: No fees, including service, dormancy or inactivity charges.

fields.label: Lost cards
fields.value: The issuer does not have to replace a lost or stolen certificate.

fields.label: Covers
fields.value: Gift certificates and gift cards for consumer goods and services. Prepaid calling cards and prepaid mobile services are not covered.
